display.title: The Four Chochmos: Rabbi Yehudah's Four Pieces of Wisdom
display.summary_short: Rabbi Yehudah spends his year's savings on four strange pieces of advice from a mysterious old man, and each one rescues him, his friend and his mitzvah of hachnasas orchim.
display.summary_long: Rabbi Yehudah always gives his guests the very best. He saves a few coins every day for a whole year so he can buy something special for them at the great Leipzig fair, and arrives with just four gold coins. Nothing he can afford is any good, until an old man in an empty shop sells him four 'chochmos', pieces of wisdom, for a coin each, and adds a warm challah as a gift. When he steps outside, the shop has vanished. On the way home each piece of advice comes true. Taking the long, bumpy road saves him, and he rescues his rich friend from robbers on the short road. Laughing at a strange sight at an inn breaks a curse and returns the governor's daughter. Leaving a hotel room shared with a priest lets him witness a murder and clear his friend in court. Holding back his anger at home spares honored guests from embarrassment. Inside the challah he finds his four gold coins and a note: the old couple were Avraham Avinu and Sarah Imeinu, rewarding his years of hachnasas orchim.
display.lesson: Give your guests the best, trust Hashem, and follow the words of a tzaddik even when you do not understand them. Never lose your temper.

advisories.note: Robbers tie up a merchant and threaten to kill him; a drunken priest stabs a man in the night; the hero cuts off the killer's finger as proof.
